newsitem.title: NORWAY: SOCCER-RAPID REKDAL HAT-TRICK SINKS HUNGARIANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAPID REKDAL HAT-TRICK SINKS HUNGARIANS.

text.p: Kjetil Rekdal scored one of international soccer's more unusual hat-tricks to secure Norway a 3-0 victory over Hungary and cement their position on top of World Cup group three on Wednesday.
The game was still level at 0-0 with seven minutes remaining when the Rennes striker finally broke the deadlock with a free-kick which pierced the Hungarian defensive wall.
He then added a second with a stunning volley from 20 metres in the 89th minute and completed a distinctly rapid hat-trick with a penalty seconds before the final whistle.
On a chilly evening at Oslo's packed Ullevaal stadium, Norway dominated the first half but were frustrated by a solid Hungarian side.

The visiting team, with forwards Tibor Balog and Tibor Dombi displaying glimpses of artistry, had an excellent spell at the start of the second half but came under increasing pressure as the game progressed.
Blackburn's Lars Bohinen, with only goalkeeper Szaboles Safar to beat in the 58th minute, shot over the crossbar from 16 meters and Ronny Johnsen of Manchester United headed a free-kick wide.

Norwegian coach Egil Olsen, whose side have won both their opening games and are the only unbeaten team in the group, said: "We did not score until the 83rd minute but I am happy justice prevailed in the end. We have played better games."
Hungarian coach Janos Csank was dissatisfied with the free-kick decision that resulted in the first goal.
"Our luck changed after a faulty ruling by the referee (Hugh Dallas of Scotland). Norway should not have had a free-kick," Csank said.

Norway - 1-Frode Grodaas, 2-Alf Inge Haaland, 3-Ronny Johnsen, 4-Henning Berg, 5-Stig Inge Bjoernebye, 6-Frank Strandli (18-Egil Oestenstad 83rd), 7-Erik Mykland, 8-Oeyvind Leonhardsen, 9-Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (17-Haavard Flo 64th), 10-Kjetil Rekdal, 11-Lars Bohinen.

Hungary - 1-Szaboles Safar, 2-Mihaly Mracsko, 3-Janos Banfi, 4-Norbert Nagy, 5-Vilmos Sebok, 6-Gabor Halmai (13-Gabor Torma 87th), 7-Tibor Balog, 8-Florian Urban, 9-Laszlo Klausz, 10-Elek Nyilas (14-Bela Illes 74th), 11-Tibor Dombi.
